newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FORECAST-Russia economy may grow in '98-World Bank.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Russia economy may grow in '98-World Bank.

text.p: Russia is slowly emerging from deep recession and can now look forward to economic growth, but significant reforms are still needed before recovery can be assured, the World Bank said on Monday.

Russia is likely to record zero growth this year, it said in an analysis, pointing to signs most Russian enterprises are in the early stages of restructuring. But current monthly trends suggest overall economic prospects have reached a turning point.

"Annual growth is expected to turn positive in 1998 and could reach six percent as a medium-term trend, driven by further expansion in services, export-oriented industries such as oil, gas and metals, and power and telecommunications sectors," it said.
Improved performance will depend on consolidating existing reforms and undertaking new structural adjustment to stimulate the private sector and address social concerns, it said.
"Over the past year, economic reform has been a hesitant process," said the World Bank's Moscow office director, Michael Carter.
He noted inflation had fallen, laying the groundwork for economic recovery.

"But at the same time you also have to overhaul the taxation system and make far-reaching reforms to capital markets, pensions, housing, regulation of natural monopolies, and privatisation, if Russia is to see its potential for rapid growth come true," he said.
Russia now needs to create the conditions for a big increase in investment, and that means restructuring the tax system to contain the fiscal deficit and help interest rates fall further.

The deficit is driven by collapsing federal tax revenues, which fell to 10 percent of gross domestic product in 1996, due to a distorted tax structure with too many taxes, a narrow tax base and high marginal rates, and to weak tax administration, with excessive exemptions and growing arrears, it said.
Russia must clarify property rights and improve its legal and regulatory systems to encourage private investment.
It must also create a strong social safety net to ease social tensions as structural reforms are undertaken, it said.
